findings.text: Three query routines expose successive words of the kernel ELF hardware capability array for userspace capability queries, covering legacy and extended sets.

Two routines provide trapped MRS emulation for identification registers, one emulating a given encoding into a destination register with fault skip, the other validating mode and opcode before decoding and attempting emulation.
A decoder extracts a register specifier from an instruction word using a per type shift and fixed width mask, reporting unknown types and returning zero for them.
A state query classifies Meltdown exposure as unaffected mitigated or vulnerable from safe flag and kernel mapping state, with a device attribute helper rendering that state as readable text.
A reporting routine logs disabled Spectre variant mitigations using a shared message suffix to avoid duplication.
Two cross file initialization routines finalize SVE and SME vector length state after system capabilities are known, deriving supported extrema defaults and virtualisable limits with logging.
Two memory initialization routines conditionally harden page tables via a system wide stop operation when hardware support and configuration require finer or non global mappings.
A signal initialization routine computes minimum signal stack size from a maximal extension layout plus frame record and alignment overhead.
Boot entry that initializes capability indirection, detects pseudo NMI support, then detects enables and patches boot CPU capabilities and alternatives.
System entry that finalizes system capabilities, adjusts linear mappings, installs isolation mappings, initializes vector extensions, and checks cache granule information.
User features entry that applies fixups, publishes native and compat ELF capabilities, and initializes minimum signal stack size.
Per CPU entry for secondaries that checks early features, then updates local capabilities before finalization or verifies conformance after finalization.
SME verification temporarily enables kernel SME access, requires agreement of the SME vector length map across CPUs, and halts the joining CPU on mismatch before restoring control state.
Hypervisor verification is skipped without KVM, otherwise it requires local VMID width to be at least the safe width and local address range to satisfy the KVM limit, halting on violation.
Partitioning verification requires matching version and hypervisor control presence and requires local partition and monitor maxima to cover system values, halting on mismatch.
Late verification excludes boot scope handled elsewhere, always checks local capabilities and ELF state, and adds vector hypervisor and partitioning checks only when the system advertises them.
System capability setup enables non boot capabilities and alternatives, then logs masked and match all capabilities plus emulated access never state and disabled Spectre mitigations.

SVE setup enforces mandatory base vector support, derives maximum length from the map, chooses a signal safe default, computes the largest virtualisable length from partial map gaps, clamps it, and warns on unvirtualisable lengths.
Vector length selection replaces invalid requested or maximum values with minima, clamps the request into supported extrema, then rounds upward to the next supported map entry.
SME setup requires at least one supported length, derives minimum and maximum from opposite ends of the shared map, validates ordering, selects a streaming safe default, and logs all three lengths.
Per vector type defaults live in a configuration table and are exchanged through single copy atomic read and write helpers wrapped by vector specific accessors.

Layout initialization zeroes state, starts used size at the reserved area, and sets the limit to cover that area minus terminator and extra context reservations, with final size rounded to sixteen byte alignment.
Record allocation pads each entry to sixteen bytes, inserts an extra context record and expands the limit to a global maximum when inline space runs out, and fails if space remains insufficient.
Finalization reclaims terminator reservation, appends a context terminator, and freezes the limit to used size to block further allocation.

Frame layout conditionally includes floating fault guarded stack vector thread pointer matrix table mode and overlay records based on system support and thread state, sizing vector and matrix entries from current or maximum lengths.
Minimum stack size derives from an all inclusive layout attempt, failing safe with a warning if the global maximum proves too small for that layout.

Asymmetric 32 bit handling records capable CPUs, treats isolated CPUs as 64 bit only, enables a mismatched branch for capable CPUs, and on first asymmetry pins a survivor online and refreshes compat capabilities.
Mismatched tracking is skipped unless allowed, allocates its CPU mask dynamically, and registers a dynamic online hotplug step, propagating allocation failure.
Only narrowly scoped system encodings are emulated, with known identification registers returning live ID safe affinity or zero and untracked registers reading as zero.
MRS emulation applies only to native 64 bit users with a genuine MRS opcode, decoding system encoding and destination from instruction fields before attempting emulation.
A Spectre variant is treated as disabled when either its specific command line flag or the global CPU mitigations off control is set.

Linear splitting runs only when level three break before make is required but unsupported, while isolation install runs only when the kernel is unmapped at low exception level without existing non global mappings.
Common not private enablement for the capability delegates to the swapper common not private activation helper.
Default vector lengths are shared without locks through single copy atomic accessors suitable for concurrent readers.
A shared page table flag is published with a write once store plus full barrier before a system wide stop operation rewrites mappings on all online CPUs.
Signal layout construction mutates only a caller supplied layout object with no locking primitives observed, implying exclusive ownership by the constructing context.
Vector length information comprises supported and partial bitmaps, minimum maximum and maximum virtualisable lengths, and a name used for logging.
Per vector type configuration holds a default length field indexed by vector kind.
User frame layout tracks used size and limit plus offsets for extra context terminator and each optional extension, with an embedded frame used only to size the reserved area.
Capability descriptors observed here carry an identifier optional description and optional CPU mask used for iteration and match checks during setup logging.
Per CPU information observed here carries the raw ID register value used to test 32 bit exception level zero support.
Initialization moves from boot detection and enablement through system detection and enablement to memory hardening vector setup cache validation and user publication.
Secondaries check early features first, then take an update path before finalization and a verification path after, with boot scope confined to the early path.
Signal layout progresses from reserved initialization through incremental allocation with optional expansion to terminator insertion and frozen final size.
Fault handling progresses from mode and opcode validation through field decode to emulation and on success destination writeback with instruction skip.
Mismatched handling moves from disabled or uninitialized to tracking online CPUs, then on first asymmetry to pinned survivor with refreshed compat state.
Any late mismatch in vector maps VMID width address range or partitioning maxima halts the joining CPU after a critical log, blocking heterogeneous bringup.
Missing mandatory vector support inverted extrema invalid length inputs absent virtualisable lengths and oversized signal maxima trigger warnings with best effort fallback values.
Record allocation can fail when padded size exceeds inline and expanded limits, aborting layout construction with out of memory status.
Emulation of out of scope encodings or unknown identification variants fails without side effects on destination or program counter.
Without pinning a survivor on asymmetry, affinity checks could reject every CPU for 32 bit tasks, so one CPU is kept online with unplug disabled.
First hardware capability word covers only low thirty two features, with bits sixty two and sixty three guaranteed zero for compatibility.
Three consecutive capability words are published as successive hardware capability levels for native queries.
SVE default length is capped at sixty four bytes and SME at thirty two bytes to preserve signal frame size, with all signal records padded to sixteen byte alignment.
SVE requires 128 bit vector support as a minimum architectural guarantee enforced during setup.
Register fields are five bits wide with shifts zero for destination and target, five for base, ten for second target and accumulator, and sixteen for source.
Emulated encodings require Op0 three CRn zero Op1 zero, with CRm zero for identification group or two through seven for feature groups.
Emulated MIDR returns live CPU identity, MPIDR returns a fixed safe value, and REVIDR plus untracked registers read as zero.
Successful emulation writes the destination register and advances past the faulting instruction by the fixed instruction size.
Meltdown reporting distinguishes unaffected mitigated via page table isolation and vulnerable outcomes with distinct human readable messages.
MRS system encoding is rebuilt from a sixteen bit immediate field shifted left by five positions.
Minimum signal stack adds rounded frame record size and sixteen bytes worst case alignment padding to the maximal layout size.
